actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The repository provides the environments used to train engineai robots to walk on rough terrain with NVIDIA's Isaac Gym and includes sim2sim and sim2real components
The package declares mujoco and mujoco-python-viewer in install_requires
Sim2simCfg points mujoco_model_path at resources/robots/zq_humanoid/urdf/zq_sa01.xml below the clone root
The MJCF root element declares the model zqsa01
The model uses radians, resolves its meshes from ../meshes/, and its option element sets timestep 0.002 s, 50 Newton iterations, gravity 0 0 -9.81 and the RK4 integrator
The world contains a plane floor and a base_link body at 0 0 1.5 that carries the free joint root
The left leg has six limited hinge joints from leg_l1_joint to leg_l6_joint, each with its own range
The right leg has six limited hinge joints from leg_r1_joint to leg_r6_joint, each with its own range
The actuator section has twelve motor actuators, one per leg hinge, each with ctrllimited true and ctrlrange -200 200
run_mujoco computes PD torques, clips them to cfg.robot_config.tau_limit and writes the result to data.ctrl
Sim2simCfg sets tau_limit to 200 for all 12 joints
Sim2simCfg sets dt to 0.001 s and decimation to 10
run_mujoco overwrites model.opt.timestep with cfg.sim_config.dt before creating MjData

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the fixed model deterministically from the model defaults; the bridge accepts a seed in cap.world.reset.v1 but a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults and does not use it, so one control sequence repeats a trajectory on the same engine.  The package's stand-in is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the MJCF for the free base, the twelve hinge joints, the twelve motor actuators, their explicit ctrlranges and the 0.002 s option step, then gives each actuated hinge a placeholder velocity proportional to its control value and holds the free base where the model puts it; it computes no inertia, torque, gravity, contact, friction, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics and produces no MuJoCo trajectory
the stand-in loads no STL mesh or texture and resolves no collision or contact; the model's floor, base collision geom and armature attributes are not applied

the upstream sim2sim loop overwrites the model time step with its own 0.001 s dt and writes PD torques, clipped to 200, to data.ctrl; this package loads the MJCF directly, serves its own 0.002 s step and takes the control vector from the caller
the fake reset restores the parsed model qpos0 and zeros; a real MjData reset also restores the full integration state, which this package did not inspect
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
no physical humanoid is modelled and nothing was validated against the ZqSA01 hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
